entities.name: Nonpurulent cellulitis
observations: Acute warm, painful, sharply demarcated erythema without fluctuance or purulence; beta-hemolytic streptococci are the most typical causes in otherwise healthy adults.

entities.name: Erysipelas
observations: A sharply demarcated superficial skin infection with fever or tachycardia, most commonly associated with beta-hemolytic streptococci, especially Group A Streptococcus.

entities.name: Group A Streptococcus
observations: Streptococcus pyogenes is the best fit for acute nonpurulent erysipelas-like cellulitis in this case.

entities.name: Staphylococcus aureus
observations: A major competing skin and soft-tissue pathogen and common cause of peripheral catheter-site infection, but more often associated with purulence, abscess, drainage, or an open wound; absence of these findings makes it less likely here.

entities.name: GAS favored over S aureus
observations: In a healthy man with nonpurulent, sharply demarcated forearm erythema and systemic inflammatory signs after a recent IV, Group A Streptococcus is favored over Staphylococcus aureus; other listed organisms require special exposures or host factors.
